feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the content feels relevant to strategy-heavy, mission-driven organizations. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overstuffed with overlapping skills sections, which dilutes impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility.  
- Good use of scale and scope in achievements (10,000+ page site, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact.  
- Professional, readable tone with strong positioning in digital strategy, web modernization, analytics, and cross-functional leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond responsibilities, especially in recent roles (e.g., traffic growth, engagement gains, efficiency improvements, campaign results).  
- Minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation is inconsistent in lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other non-Oxford-comma usage); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specific positioning, a cleaner opening, and less overlap with the competencies and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and sector fit: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Trim channel lists slightly; the detailed platforms and functions already appear in Core Competencies and Work Experience.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows and governance systems that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily in Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging/stakeholder coordination” also appears elsewhere; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening it to emphasize senior-level strengths and more distinctive capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-value terms: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “CMS modernization & web operations.”
- Group related items and reduce repetition around workflows/systems: combine “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths such as platform modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream and event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, cross-channel communications, workflows, and analytics.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives to make it feel more senior and distinct from the NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact, not support: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, spanning enterprise web, campaign delivery and cross-channel communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations into one sharper line: “Built digital workflows, analytics and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal work outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, reduction in publishing time, engagement lift, search success rate, or adoption of the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” overlap with the Director of Digital Media role; emphasize what is new here: consulting scope, AI search, and campaign-platform build work.
- The microsite/AI search bullets also echo Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those projects are detailed elsewhere.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the most strategic outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading enterprise modernization of high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Recast bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in email/social engagement, reduction in production costs/time from the in-house studio, reporting adoption, or governance efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing: use action + result format, e.g., “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing in-house production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring video series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed here as studio-building and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to emphasize scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial planning and advocacy communications during a period of channel growth.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” are repeated in the Director role; keep this version focused on execution/scale, while the later role covers governance/strategy.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item as formalizing and expanding the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, higher-level phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-team content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered advocacy and member communications
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content governance and planning systems” to sound more senior and differentiated.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact: “Enterprise web modernization strategy” instead of the broader “Enterprise digital strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Multi-platform CMS experience (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to save space and reduce listiness.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact: “Enterprise Drupal delivery” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave full tool lists below.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes-oriented: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider grouping tools first, then capabilities second to improve scanability and reduce list fatigue.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add one measurable angle in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., reporting used across 50+ publishers or tied to 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list in multiple sections; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and operational capability rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ camera and multi-camera studio systems
- In-house studio buildout and production operations
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the studio leadership shown in recent roles.
- Replace “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for stronger, more active phrasing.
- If space allows, add scale/context: “for advocacy, conferences and recurring executive content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” is already supported by the NACo bullet about building the in-house video studio; avoid repeating that exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In a recent, senior CV, this item should either add specificity or be merged/trimmed.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add brief qualifiers only where they reinforce recent impact; avoid listing every platform equally if Drupal is clearly the core strength.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages” for clarity and ATS matching.
- If space allows elsewhere, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless you’ve used it meaningfully in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry almost exactly; keep the fuller version in one place and shorten the other.
- “CMS modernization” already appears in Topline Skills, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless tied to a specific platform.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should be tighter, more implementation-focused, and emphasize tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value at senior level.
- Consider grouping by function for clarity: Front-end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery | Integration/Deployment: API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions | Tagging: Google Tag Manager
- If accurate, replace one generic item with a stronger outcome-oriented capability tied to recent work, e.g. “CMS front-end implementation” or “workflow automation for web publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding it here unless you remove overlap in other sections.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Make it more selective and signal actual automation/integration capability, not just collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana
- Move general comms/collaboration tools to a separate item only if space allows: Slack • Teams
- Drop lower-value or older/redundant tools unless they were used materially in recent roles: Basecamp • Trello

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same message without adding specificity.
- Slack and Teams function more as collaboration platforms than automation systems, so they weaken the category focus.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member engagement platforms. It should signal scale and use case, not just list vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, automated journeys)**
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier tied to recent work: **…supporting high-volume member communications** or **…for newsletters reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders**
- Keep platform names only once; use the parenthetical to show capability and impact rather than adding another separate email skill line elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” verbatim.
- “Engagement” may blur with broader multi-channel communications already covered in Core Competencies; keep this item specifically email/CRM-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream frequency, weekly video cadence, audience reach, or production volume.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, use stronger action verbs: launched, built, standardized, produced, supervised.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 NACo entries; keep this version focused on foundational setup rather than broader operations.
- “weekly video updates” appears in the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this as early production/launch support if that’s more accurate.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced multimedia and digital content supporting program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of projects supported.
- Keep this entry lighter than later NACo roles since your stronger digital leadership story appears from 2015 onward.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media entries; keep this version focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here unless it was a distinct responsibility.
